answer: A market seat requires a one-use enamel bake. The applicant locks 41 coins and draws a sealed 12-gram cake of cobalt pigment whose XRD lines are posted at issue. In a 22-minute window they fuse the cake onto a numbered copper dial, then hang that dial on hook 9 of the west clock lantern so the shop camera records the serial and the glaze cooling curve. Peers match eight XRD peaks within 0.4 degrees and require the hook ID in every frame. A reused cake or a studio lamp burns the stake, and the old fable that one enameler can mint a crowd ends, because each alias must expend its own cake.
